The petitioner has filed this petition under section 397 of
Code of Criminal Procedure to direct the respondent to de-freeze
the current account of the petitioner bearing
No.0009102000081360 of I.D.I.B.I. Bank, C.G.Road Branch,
Gujarat in connection with Crime No.413/2021 of Cyber Crime
Police Station Central Cell Bangalore for the offences punishable
U/s.419, 420 of Indian Penal Code and Sec.66 D of Information
Technology Act 2008 and also to release back the amount of
Rs.1,12,15,884/- which was taken from the account of the
petitioner to him in the interest of justice.

2. The brief facts of the case as narrated by the petitioner is
that the petitioner is a proprietary concern and he is the
representative of the said concern.

The petitioner companies
proprietor is a person who is highly respected in the society and
 3 C.R.P.No.475/2022
belong to a very respectful and cultural family.

The defacto
complainant company by name M/s.Chandru and Co., received
a call from an unknown number saying that they are willing to
offer a business deal which would yield great profits and
business was for Exporting Biochampacalin Fluid to Uk.

After
receiving the mail, the complainant contacted them and the
business deal was that to procure Biochampacalin Fluid from
M/s. Sagar Enterprises and export the same to Centric Pharma
situated in Uk.

In respect of the aforesaid business transaction
a sum of Rs.3,00,000/- was transferred on 22.07.2021 to M/s.
Sagar Enterprises as an advance for purchasing 1 liter of sample
fluid.

Later, on 05.08.2021 a sum of Rs.30,00,000/- was
transferred to Hdfc Bank and sum of Rs.27,00,000/- was
transferred to Dbs Bank

and on 10.08.2021 a sum of
Rs.30,00,000/- was transferred to Dbs Bank belonging to M/s.
Sagar Enterprises by the defacto complainant.

On 10.08.2021, a
sum of Rs.27,00,000/- was transferred to the current account of
petitioner herein with Idbi Bank, C.G.Road Branch Ahmedabad
by the defacto complainant.

After transferring the amount of
Rs.1,17,00,000/-, M/s.Sagar Enterprises, they have cheated the
complainant by not supplying fluid.

Therefore, a complaint came
to be filed against M/s.Sagar Enterprises.

Respondent police
based on the complaint of the defacto complainant, during the

course of investigation have frozen the Bank account pertaining
to the petitioner as per the chart herein below:

Holder Bank Number Code

Mahi Idbi Bank 000910200 Ibkl00 Rs.1,12,15,884/-

3.

The Police seized and deposited Rs.1,12,15,884/- from the
account of the petitioner and released the same to the
complainant.

The learned Magistrate rejected the application
filed by the petitioner U/s.451 and 457 of Code of Criminal
Procedure.

Aggrieved by the said order dated 18.05.2022, the
petitioner has come up with this revision petition.

On the
following;
 Grounds
 (i) The petitioner is a dutiful and law-abiding citizen by
complying tax liabilities in respect of business transaction.

There
is no connection or business between the petitioner and M/s.
Sagar Enterprises and the petitioner was operating the said
account for business purpose.

The petitioner is unaware about
the transaction between the complainant and Sagar Enterprises.
 (ii) The complaint averments does not disclose any
offence committed by the petitioner.

The complainant with the
malafide intention has filed the complaint against the petitioner.

There is no contract or an agreement or communication between
the petitioner and complainant.

5 C.R.P.No.475/2022
 (iii) The petitioner is not involved in any fraudulent
transactions and the Complainant Police proceeded to freeze the
account of the petitioner and seized cash of Rs.1,12,15,884/-
under PF.No.14/2021 which exclusively belongs to the
petitioner.

(iv) The amount freezed by the Police is the hard-earned
money of the petitioner and the petitioner is involved in a
business which yields him Crores of Rupees on a daily basis.

If
the petition is not allowed, he would be put to great hardship
and loss.

(v) Petitioner is ready to abide by the conditions,
Mahi Enterprises Rept By Parikh Bhavik vs Central Cen Ps on 11 November, 2024
Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/113456196/
3

imposed by this Court, the petitioner will not utilize the account
for any other purpose and also support the Investigating Officer
and will not destroy any evidence.

(vi) The defacto complainant has not provided any proof
or documents before the Trial Court that the petitioner has
induced the Defacto Complainant to believe him and transfer
huge amount of Rs.1,17,00,000/- fraudulently.

It is the mistake
of the defacto Complainant that he failed to verify the call of un-
known number and agreed to enter into business with them
with the greedy intention to fetch huge profits.

(vii) The complainant has produced a Gst number of M/s
Sagar Enterprises which was in the email and the same does not
 6 C.R.P.No.475/2022
belong to Mahi Enterprises.

The petitioner is carrying on
business relating to Agro-Based products and hence the Gst
will not be applicable to such business.

4. On the above among other grounds the petitioner prayed
to allow the application.

5. The learned Public Prosecutor has resisted the application
by filing detailed objections wherein it is stated that application
filed by the petitioner is not maintainable and the same is liable
to be rejected.

The learned Trial Court has correctly rejected the
application filed by the petitioner.

There are prima facie
materials to show that by inducing the complainant to pay the
money, the petitioner has supplied fake Biochampacilin Fluid.

A
sum of Rs.1,17,00,000/- was transferred from the account of
the complainant.

There are materials to show that request was
made to transfer the amount to the account of Mahi Enterprises.

The said amount being the proceeds of the Crime on the
permission of the learned Magistrate Demand Draft was
obtained and deposited before the court in turn the learned
Magistrate released the same in favour of the complainant on
certain conditions.

If the account of the petitioner is de-freezed
there are chances of committing similar offences.

Therefore,
prayed for dismissal of the application.

6. Respondent No.2 has not filed any objections to the
petition filed by the petitioner.

sentences.text:
Heard the arguments of the learned counsel for petitioner and
respondents.

8. Having heard the learned counsel for petitioner and
respondents and on going through the material placed on
record

, the points that arises for my consideration are:-
 1.

Whether the petitioner has made out
 grounds to set aside the order dated
 18/05/2022 of the learned
 Magistrate passed in Crime.
 No.413/2021 of Cem Police Station
 and to direct the Respondent Police to
 return back the amount in favour of
 the petitioner and release the amount
 to the petitioner as sought for ?
2. What order?

9. My answer to the above points are.-
 Point No.1:- In the Negative
 Point No.2:- As per final order
 for the following;
 Reasons
10. Point No.1 :- The petitioner has filed this revision petition
challenging the order dated 18/05/2022 in Crime No.413/2013
on the file of I Acmm, Bengaluru passed on application under
Section 451 and 457 of Cr.P.C by petitioner/ accused No.3.
 8 C.R.P.No.475/2022
11.

The counsel for respondent No.2 has vehemently argued
regarding the maintainability of the revision petition before this
Court.

He has categorically stated that since the application is
made for interim custody of the amount before the trial Court,
the revision petition is not maintainable.

Though I find some
force in the arguments advanced by the counsel for respondent,
it is to be noted that the counsel for petitioner has relied upon a
ruling reported in Criminal Revision Petition 100268/2023 in
the case of Mustafa vs State of Karnataka wherein the Hon'ble
High Court of Karnataka relying upon various judgments held
that when the revision petition is decided against the petitioner,
he has got a right to prefer revision petition against that order
which cannot be construed as an interlocutory order for the
purpose of Section 397 of Cr.P.C.

In view of the finding in the
above said judgment, it is to be considered that the revision
petition of this nature is maintainable.

12. The petitioner has challenged the order of the learned
Mahi Enterprises Rept By Parikh Bhavik vs Central Cen Ps on 11 November, 2024

Magistrate in dismissing the application filed by him under
Section 451 and 457 of Cr.P.C for release of the amount seized
by the police to the tune of Rs.1,12,15,884/- under Pf No.14/21
of Cen Police Station.

The contention of the petitioner is that
the defacto complainant transferred a sum of Rs.27,00,000/- in
favour of the petitioner company.

The rest of the amount seized
by the police is the hard earned money of the petitioner and
therefore the learned Magistrate ought not to have rejected the
 9 C.R.P.No.475/2022
application filed by the petitioner.

Though I find some force in
the arguments advanced by the counsel for petitioner, it is to be
noted that the available materials on record indicates that the
petitioner is none other than the associate of the accused No.1
who entered into agreement with the defacto complainant and to
whom the amount was transferred from the defacto
complainant.
13.

I have perused the materials placed before the Court
wherein it indicates that on the basis of the request of Sagar
Enterprises along with whom the defacto complainant had
transaction, the amount was transferred to the account of Mahi
Enterprises.

The email communication to that effect placed on
record clearly indicates the said fact.

Apart from the above the
objections filed by the learned Public Prosecutor indicates that
the case came to be registered against the petitioner by Bhopal
Police in connection with similar offence.

Therefore, it has to be
ascertained whether the petitioner is jointly operating with Sagar
Enterprises.

This can be ascertained only after a full fledged
trial.

At this stage the available material on record indicates
that the defacto complainant has transferred the amount to the
account of Sagar Enterprises and Mahi Enterprises.

Therefore
the fact that the amount which is deposited in the account of the
petitioner being proceeds of the crime cannot be ruled out.
Further same can be ascertained after a full fledged trial.

It is
also not in dispute that the complainant has lost a sum of
 10 C.R.P.No.475/2022
Rs.1,17,00,000/- by transferring it to the account of the
petitioner and Sagar Enterprises.

Since there is every possibility
that the amount deposited in the account of the petitioner being
proceeds of the crime, I find no fault in the order of the learned
Magistrate in releasing the amount seized under Pf No.14/2021
in favour of the defacto complainant who actually lost the
amount
due to the fraudulent act of the Sagar Enterprises as
well as
the petitioner.

14.

The counsel for petitioner has also advanced his
arguments that the account of the petitioner is freezed by the
bank on the request of the concerned police and no purpose
would be served by freezing the account.

He is transacting his
business through the said account and he requires the said
account for day today transaction and therefore sought to de-
freeze the said account and also challenged the order of learned
Magistrate in dismissing the said application.

It is not in
dispute that the defacto complainant has transferred the
amount to the account of the petitioner.

When the documents
are available in proof of the same, it is not forthcoming and not
explained as to why a situation arose to defraud the defacto
complainant on the part of the petitioner.

15. Apart from the above there are also materials to show that
the petitioner is involved in similar offences and the Bhopal
police are in search of the petitioner and they have also sought
 11 C.R.P.No.475/2022
for freezing of the account of the petitioner.

Under these
circumstances if an order of de-freezing the account of the
petitioner is passed, definitely there are chances of the petitioner
committing similar offence and there are also chances of
destroying of material evidence.
Further it may also come in the
way of proper investigation of this case as well as case registered
by Bhopal Police

. Under these circumstances the reason
assigned by the learned Magistrate dismissing the application
filed for de-freezing the account of the petitioner does not suffer
from any infirmity.

16. The learned counsel for the petitioner has vehemently
argued that before freeing of account and deposits of the amount
standing in his account before the trial Court and prior to
release of the same to the defacto complainant, notice has not
been issued to the petitioner.

17. I have gone through the materials produced by the
petitioner himself before the Court which indicates that Cen
Police, Central Division have issued notice under Section 41(a) of
Cr.P.C to the proprietor of M/s. Mahi Enterprises on
14/9/2021, 23/9/2021, 25/9/2021, but the petitioner has not
responded to the said notice issued by the Io.

When the
petitioner has not responded to the notice issued to him by the
Io, he is estopped from taking a plea that notice was not issued
to him before release of the amount in favour of the defacto
Mahi Enterprises Rept By Parikh Bhavik vs Central Cen Ps on 11 November, 2024
Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/113456196/
7

 12 C.R.P.No.475/2022
complainant.

In support of his contention the counsel for
petitioner has relied upon a judgment passed by the Hon'ble
High Court of Karnataka in Wp No.2865/2022 (Gm-Res) in
the case of Sri. Rahul Chari and another vs State of
Karnataka and others, wherein the order of the learned
Magistrate in releasing the amount to the complainant was set
aside.

entities.text:
Sri. Rahul Chari and another vs State of
Karnataka and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
18. I have gone through the findings given in the said
judgment wherein it indicates that in the said case the petitioner
was not an accused.

He was not aware of the registration of the
case.

Without he being the accused his account was freezed and
amount was released in favour of the defacto complainant.

19. In the said case, the petitioner was only an account holder
and not an accused.

Under the said circumstances the Hon'ble
High Court passed an order to issue notice to the account holder
and set aside the order of the learned Magistrate.

The relevant
portion of the judgment of the Hon'ble High Court is extracted
below:
 "This Court is coming across scores and
 scores of cases where the account is frozen,
 defrozen and the amount that the complainant is
 due from a suspect or an accused is transferred to
 the account of the complainant from the account of
 13 C.R.P.No.475/2022
 third parties which action is contrary to all cannons
 of law".

But unlike the said case in this case the account does not
belong to third party, but account belong to the petitioner and

the said amount was ordered to be released in favour of the
defacto complainant.

Under these circumstances, the ruling
relied upon by the learned counsel for petitioner is not
applicable to the facts and circumstances of this case.

20. The learned counsel for respondent No.2 has argued to
the effect that the order passed by the learned Magistrate is
proper.

He has argued that the petitioner is none other than the
accused in this case.

Under these circumstances the order
Mahi Enterprises Rept By Parikh Bhavik vs Central Cen Ps on 11 November, 2024
Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/113456196/
8

passed by the learned Magistrate is just and proper.

In support
of his contention, the learned counsel for respondent No.2 has
relied upon judgment reported in Ilr 1984 Karnataka 923 in
the case of Mangharam and sons vs. R.C.Morzaria and
another wherein it is held that :
 "In a case like this where the person from whom
 the property is seized also claims the custody of that
 property, two things are required to be considered.

entities.text:
Mangharam and sons vs. R.C.Morzaria and
another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Normally the person from whom the property is seized
 is entitled to the custody of the same (with or without
 conditions) but he will not be entrusted with the
 property if there is prima facie material on record
 14 C.R.P.No.475/2022
 showing that he has committed some offence re: the
 same.

In such an event, the claim, if any, of the other
 person, or the complainant as in this case, may be
 considered.

While examining the rival claims the
 question as to who was in lawful possession firstly,
 at the time of seizure and secondly, earlier that is to
 say, earlier to the event which gave cause to that
 seizure, is very important.

If no prima facie case for
 any offence is made out against the person from
 whom the property is seized he can be presumed to
 have been in lawful possession of the same as the
 time of seizure and may be entrusted with it."
21.

I have perused the orders passed by the learned Magistrate
wherein it is stated that the petitioner who is accused No.3 has
not appeared before the Io despite issuance of repeated notices
nor he has put-forth any documents to show his accumulation
of aforesaid huge amount by lawful means by producing
amounts of his firm.

It further shows that he has not co-
operated with investigation and all these aspects raises doubt
regarding his claim towards aforesaid freezed amount.

The
learned Magistrate also held that the online copy of Gst status,
wherein the Gst number of petitioner shown in email of the
complainant is shown as invalid.

He has also discussed
regarding the involvement of the petitioner in this case.

Considering all the above aspects the learned Magistrate has
 15 C.R.P.No.475/2022
 rightly rejected the application filed by the petitioner and I find
 no ground to interfere with the orders passed by the learned
 Magistrate.

sentences.text:
On perusal of the materials placed before the Court and
 orders passed by the learned Magistrate there is nothing on
 record to come to a conclusion that correctness, legality or
 proprietary of the findings recorded by the trial Court suffers
 from all the infirmities.

It is to be noted that the amount was
 released to the interim custody of the defacto complainant.

There are all the opportunities for the petitioner to put forward
 his claim during the conclusion of the trial.

Therefore I find no
 reason to interfere with the finding of the learned trial Court.
Therefore, the point No.1 is answered in the negative.
23. Point No.2:-

In the result I proceed to pass the following:-
 Order
The petition filed by the petitioners under Section 397(3) of Code of Criminal Procedure Code is
hereby
dismissed with cost.
